title: Liquidity, Shutdowns, Tariffs, and Earnings
summary: Tariff incidence, liquidity and payment balance sheets.
coverage_note: All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

claims.reason: The February 20, 2026 decision came before June and rejected IEEPA tariff authority. This supports the reported court-watchers timing scenario; the article did not itself make an unqualified directional ruling forecast.

evidence.title: Learning Resources v Trump
evidence.finding: Court held that IEEPA does not authorize presidential tariffs, following November 5, 2025 argument. The decision arrived before June 2026 and did not itself establish the net fiscal effect of replacement measures.

claims.reason: Observed gradual consumer price pass-through supports the distinction between importer remittance and economic burden. Foreign pricing, domestic margins and consumer prices can share the effect over time.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: Gradual tariff pass-through in 2025
evidence.finding: Five-retailer price data show gradual 2025 pass-through; goods imported from China were 8.5% higher year over year in December, with at least 30% tariff pass-through April-December. Coverage is not all consumer spending.

claims.reason: The direction of increasing pass-through is supported. The cited Goldman 55% consumer burden by year-end is a specific model forecast and cannot be verified by a different study percentage with different coverage.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: Q4 2025 GDP second estimate
evidence.finding: BEA estimated reduced federal services during the shutdown subtracted about one percentage point from Q4 annualized real GDP growth. This is a specific quarterly effect, not a permanent one-percent GDP loss.

evidence.title: October 2025 implementation note
evidence.finding: Fed ended aggregate securities runoff December 1, 2025, rolling Treasury maturities and reinvesting agency principal into Treasury bills.

claims.reason: Research supports approximate satiation thresholds, not an immutable bank-cash ratio. Shifting reserve demand, distribution and nonreserve cash holdings limit a mechanical $3 trillion rule.

evidence.title: Time-varying reserve demand curve
evidence.finding: Study estimates reserve satiation above 12-13% of bank assets using 2010-24 data. Reserve demand shifts over time; the estimate is not a binding fixed regulatory minimum.

claims.reason: The Fed announced purchases in December 2025, before the first-half-2026 deadline, explicitly for ample reserves. Correct direction and policy label; earlier start than the central timing discussed.
claims.timing_assessment: Original horizon retained: first half of 2026
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: Reserve management purchases statement
evidence.finding: Fed directed purchases of Treasury bills, or maturities up to three years if needed, to maintain ample reserves. Initial reserve-management purchases began in December 2025.

claims.reason: A TGA increase drains reserves when other Fed liabilities and assets are held constant. Attributing the entire overshoot to the shutdown needs daily receipts, outlays and borrowing data; the accounting identity does not identify that cause.

claims.reason: Issuer results confirm materially weaker earnings, cash generation and reset guidance. This is an explicit update to the earlier sentiment-heavy interpretation. Alleged prior management intent is not established by a miss alone.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.

evidence.title: Fiserv Q3 2025 results and guidance reset
evidence.finding: Q3 organic revenue grew 1%; adjusted EPS fell 11% to $2.04 and nine-month free cash flow fell to $2.88 billion from $3.34 billion. Management reset full-year organic growth to 3.5-4% and adjusted EPS to $8.50-8.60.

claims.reason: For fixed debt, a given enterprise-value loss is a larger percentage loss of equity. Net debt divided by net income is not a standard debt-service coverage measure; cash flow, EBITDA, maturities and covenants are needed.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

claims.reason: By Q3 2026 revenue and adjusted earnings remained weak and goodwill was impaired, adverse to an easy recovery. No exact turnaround date was promised, and the decision was to wait before adding.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: Fiserv Q3 2026 results
evidence.finding: Q3 revenue fell 1%, organic revenue was flat, adjusted EPS $1.75 versus prior $2.04, and a $6.45 billion goodwill impairment produced GAAP loss. Nine-month operating cash flow fell to $3.09 billion from $4.12 billion.

claims.reason: Later cash and investments exceeded debt, supporting lower financing risk. Net income is not freely available cash, so four months of accounting profit cannot automatically retire debt after reinvestment and restricted funds.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.

evidence.title: PayPal Q3 2026 results
evidence.finding: Revenue grew 2%, GAAP EPS fell 4%, adjusted EPS rose 8%. Cash, equivalents and investments were $15.1 billion versus $13.5 billion debt. Quarterly free cash flow was $1.4 billion; reported and adjusted metrics differ.

claims.reason: Q3 2026 showed modest revenue growth and higher adjusted EPS, but lower GAAP earnings and an adverse share-price sensitivity. Some progress is visible; a durable successful transformation has no specified completion criterion.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.
